keywords.def: sun letters: the laam of al- is not said, the next letter doubles
moon letters: the laam of al- is said clearly
an alif said only when we start on it

questions.q: Read «فَيُعَذِّبُهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَكْبَرَ» (88:24) and name each al-.
questions.a: ٱللَّهُ: the Name Allah (next lesson); ٱلْعَذَابَ: moon (ع); ٱلْأَكْبَرَ: moon (ء).

questions.q: Laam audit (pupil PDF): underline every al- in 88:17 to 26 and write S or M. Today's rota group recites 88:17 to 21 in turn.
questions.a: M ٱلْإِبِلِ, S ٱلسَّمَآءِ, M ٱلْجِبَالِ, M ٱلْأَرْضِ, M ٱلْعَذَابَ, M ٱلْأَكْبَرَ (ٱللَّهُ: the Name of Allah).

questions.q: Extend: find two sun-letter words in Al-Fatihah.
questions.a: ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ, ٱلرَّحِيمِ, ٱلدِّينِ, ٱلصِّرَٰطَ, ٱلضَّآلِّينَ (any two).

questions.q: Stretch: why is «ٱلَّيْلِ» written with a shaddah on the laam?
questions.a: The laam of al- merges into the first laam of layl (a sun letter), so one laam with shaddah.

questions.q: In «وَإِلَى ٱلْجِبَالِ» (88:19), how do we join it?
questions.a: A) wa ilal-jibaal. Joining from before, the alif of al- is silent and the long 'aa' of إِلَىٰ is shortened before it; ج is a moon letter so the laam is said.

questions.q: When we join from the word before, the alif of al- is ...
Think again: Is it easier to spot a rule on its own or in a whole ayah? Why do we need to practise both?
questions.a: On its own is easier; in recitation we must notice rules while keeping the flow. Practice joins the two.
